state.background: Review the implementation checkpoint for the updated plan at results/plan46/phase6/browser-context-settings-commonization-plan-2026-09-29.md, using the Stage 0 inventory at results/plan46/phase6/browser-context-settings-commonization-stage0-inventory-2026-09-29.md. The inventory defines the population as 22 unique BrowserCommand implementations and 25 implementation × provider rows (22 Chromium, plus WebKit variants for batch4-b, batch5-standard, and batch5-lazy-tabs). B01/B02 call the already-counted inspectPhase5Rendering implementation. The migration uses context-only withIsolatedContext(browser, options, callback): commands retain Browser/provider acquisition and checks, page creation, routing, waits, assertions, command-specific I/O, skip/failure behavior, and scenario flow. The helper creates one independent context per invocation, runs the callback, and attempts exactly one close after context creation. A newContext failure has no close; callback/page failure preserves and propagates the original thrown value, identity, and stack while retaining close failure as supplemental information; close-only failure propagates. Option builders return fresh top-level options and copy mutable viewport/screen nested objects; device descriptors are preserved in full and merged before scenario overrides. No generic deep clone, context pooling/reuse, navigation/wait/assertion abstraction, or performance claim is part of the change. Migration groups cover the seven simple Chromium commands (next-route-poc, B03/B04/B05, B07/B08/B09), representative device/scenario cases (B10 and B14), and remaining B06/B11/B12/B13, Phase 5 rendering/interaction, batch1, batch3-a/b, batch4-a/b, and batch5-standard/lazy-tabs commands, with shared Chromium/WebKit commands migrated and checked last. The specification synchronizes Data Sources, Data Flow, Component Tree, and Requirements/WHEN-THEN scenarios for independent context lifecycle, error handling, provider/command boundaries, and descriptor-to-scenario override order. vitest.config.ts retains an exact-path default-suite exclusion for the independent Phase 4 Browser Mode probe; Browser Mode remains tested by its dedicated configuration. This is a maintainability and cleanup-reliability change: context/page creation counts are unchanged, so runtime improvement is not claimed.
acceptanceCriteria: The Stage 0 inventory and implementation reconcile to 22 unique command implementations and 25 provider rows, with B01/B02 treated as callers of inspectPhase5Rendering and the three WebKit variants counted separately.

withIsolatedContext is context-only and limited to creating one independent context from the supplied Browser, running the callback, and closing the context once; Browser acquisition, provider decisions, route/page work, command inputs/outputs, waits, assertions, and skip/failure behavior remain command-owned.

All lifecycle paths meet the stated error contract: no close after newContext failure; exactly one close attempt after context creation, including callback/newPage failure; original callback error identity and stack are preserved and propagated when close also fails, with the close error retained as supplemental information; close-only failure propagates.

Option builders return fresh top-level options and fresh copies of mutable nested viewport/screen objects, preserve the complete device descriptor, and apply scenario overrides after the descriptor without generic deep cloning.

All planned migration groups are represented: seven simple Chromium commands; B10/B14 representative device/scenario commands; remaining B06/B11/B12/B13, Phase 5 rendering and interaction, batch1, batch3-a/b, batch4-a/b, and batch5-standard/lazy-tabs; shared Chromium/WebKit variants are handled last.

The updated specification synchronizes Data Sources, Data Flow, Component Tree, and Requirements with WHEN/THEN scenarios for context lifecycle and cleanup, exception behavior, command/provider boundaries, and option merge order.

The default Vitest suite keeps the targeted exact-path exclusion for the independent Phase 4 Browser Mode probe, while dedicated Browser Mode and built route configurations continue to cover their respective test populations.
Verification evidence supports the implementation as recorded, and no runtime improvement or causal performance claim is inferred from these runs.
verification: After the unrelated CpiChart type issue was fixed, pnpm run lint:fast, pnpm run type-check, the isolated-context helper unit tests, and pnpm run test:all passed. The first test:all attempt failed in the independent Phase 4 Browser Mode probe; adding that probe's exact-path exclusion to the default vitest.config.ts allowed the final test:all run to pass.
pnpm run test:browser passed: 22 files, 74 passed, 6 skipped.
The full built route suite passed on Chromium: 22 files, 97 passed, approximately 329.94 seconds; WebKit: 4 files, 14 passed, 5 skipped, approximately 83.08 seconds.
The focused Phase 5 interaction Browser Mode run passed: 1 file, 2 tests.
Focused built route runs passed for B10 (3 tests) and B14 (4 tests).
A code review of the migrated commands and helper found no functional mismatch with the prior command behavior or the updated plan.
knownConstraints: The helper preserves a new independent BrowserContext per invocation and does not reduce context or page creation counts; the recorded durations are validation observations, not evidence of a speedup.
The full built route run took approximately 329.94 seconds for Chromium and 83.08 seconds for WebKit in these runs; these single-run observations do not establish general performance or causality.

The initial test:all failure was isolated to the independent Phase 4 Browser Mode probe and was resolved for the default suite by an exact-path exclusion; the dedicated Browser Mode configuration remains a separate validation gate.
